images.caption: Figure 1:CEPO separates coordination and execution for role-aligned prompt optimization.(a) Prior work vs. CEPO (left).Existing methods couple coordination and execution roles within agent-specific prompts. CEPO represents these functions as distinct optimizable parameters through a shared coordinator promptpCp_{C}and agent-specific executor promptspEp_{E}, and guides their updates according to their respective roles using an existing prompt optimizer.(b) Component-wise comparison (right).Accuracy on MDocAgent(Han et al., 2025a)+ MMLongBench-Doc(Ma et al., 2024). Vanilla optimizer improves baseline (54.1→57.954.1\to 57.9), prompt decomposition yields a further gain (58.658.6), and combining decomposition with role-aligned optimization (CEPO) performs the best (61.061.0).

Figure 2:Overview of CEPO.CEPO decomposes prompts within a multi-agent system into two layers with distinct roles. Thecoordinator promptpCp_{C}(top), shared across all agents, captures coordination signals (team composition, role assignment, and shared norms for reasoning). Eachexecutor promptpE(i)p_{E}^{(i)}(bottom), local to agentAiA_{i}, captures execution signals (evidence anchoring, task scoping, and procedure execution). The effective prompt forAiA_{i}is the concatenationpC⊕pE(i)p_{C}\oplus p_{E}^{(i)}. Two layers are sequentially optimized with role-aligned guidance under CEPO: the coordinator is optimized using meta-instructionΦC\Phi_{C}with executors fixed (Phase 1), then executors are optimized usingΦE\Phi_{E}with the coordinator fixed (Phase 2). CEPO applies these design principles to existing prompt optimizers𝒪\mathcal{O}, consistently improving those methods.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison of optimized prompts.Through optimization, the coordinator prompt evolves from a generic description into team-level orchestration rules. The executor prompt ofGENERALagent evolves from vague instructions into a concrete agent-level execution procedure.
